question: Should OpenClaw accept the RFC's opt-in canonical readiness contract, including its activation boundary, required/advisory semantics, subject identity model, and plugin-provider lifecycle?
rationale: These choices define new configuration and plugin-facing behavior; source review cannot determine whether they fit the intended long-term Gateway and extension contract.

options.title: Decide the v1 readiness boundary
options.body: Record maintainer acceptance or requested narrowing of the activation, aggregation, identity, and provider rules before this RFC merges.

options.title: Defer the proposal
options.body: Keep the RFC in draft until Gateway and plugin owners can sponsor a narrower or different readiness direction.

recommendation.title: Decide the v1 readiness boundary
recommendation.body: Record maintainer acceptance or requested narrowing of the activation, aggregation, identity, and provider rules before this RFC merges.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the best available routing contact for the RFC and can incorporate the recorded decision, although product acceptance remains a maintainer choice.
